title: X Feed Digest
summary: OpenAI dominated the AI side of the feed: a real Codex pricing shift is landing, while GPT-5.5/"Spud" speculation is heating up expectations for the next model cycle.
The highest-signal AI posts were less about hype and more about operating discipline — spec-first workflows, smaller task slices, stronger prompt framing, and cheaper agent loops.
Browser-native agents and agent-security concerns are converging: people are excited about thinner DOM-based automation, but increasingly aware that web agents are easy to poison or misdirect.

On markets, the most interesting angle was not a single macro print but a cluster of signs around crypto entering mainstream rails and a growing thesis that consumer spending is softening beneath the surface.

items.title: @LLMJunky: Codex Pricing Goes Token-Based
items.body: A widely shared post says OpenAI is shifting Codex workspace credits away from coarse message buckets and toward token-based billing, with Business and newer Enterprise accounts already seeing the change. The practical implication is better granularity for light tasks, but much easier cost blow-ups for heavy agentic workloads.

items.title: @chenchengpro: Agent Skills as Engineering Discipline
items.body: A detailed thread on Addy Osmani’s open-source Agent Skills argues the next frontier is not clever prompting but encoded process: write specs first, ship in vertical slices, test continuously, and explicitly block AI shortcut-taking. It reads like a real attempt to turn good engineering habits into reusable operating constraints for coding agents.

items.title: @Suryanshti777: In-Page GUI Agents
items.body: A demo-heavy post around page-agent.js suggests browser automation may get much thinner: instead of external stacks, a page can expose its own DOM to an LLM and accept natural-language actions from inside the app. If the underlying project is solid, this points to a lightweight pattern for AI copilots in SaaS and internal tools.

items.title: @blackanger: Stop Policing Tone, Start Framing the Job
items.body: One of the better workflow notes in the batch argues that if a coding agent feels too deferential, the fix is not banning phrases but giving it a stronger contract: finish a complete unit of work and justify decisions after the fact. Useful prompt-design takeaway: bind the model to task completion, not to constantly managing the user’s feelings.

items.title: @WatcherGuru: Crypto Moves Closer to Mainstream Rails
items.body: The most actionable market recap in the feed centered on crypto financialization: possible 401(k) access for alternative assets, Schwab preparing BTC/ETH trading, and Coinbase advancing toward trust-company infrastructure. Even allowing for headline compression in recap threads, the direction of travel is clear — crypto exposure is being packaged in more conventional wrappers.

items.title: @fannaoxiaoyang: Consumer Weakness Beneath the Surface
items.body: A sharp macro thread connected cheaper Apple and Tesla product pushes with Costco’s Kirkland gains to argue that North American middle-class spending power is deteriorating before markets have fully priced it. It is more mosaic theory than hard data release, but it was one of the more thoughtful reads on the tape.

items.title: @_FORAB: Ackman Uses X as a Capital-Markets Battlefield
items.body: A Chinese-language summary of Bill Ackman’s public employment dispute stood out because it treats X not as gossip but as strategy: layoffs, legal claims, reputation risk, and IPO positioning are all being fought in public. The broader lesson is that executive communication is now part of the deal and litigation playbook, not just PR.

items.title: @binghe: A Better Workflow for AI-Generated UI
items.body: A practical UI workflow got traction: use one model to turn product requirements into a sharper design brief, generate mockups in a design-focused tool, then hand the refined visuals into an interactive builder. The point is less which tool wins and more that separating product thinking, design generation, and implementation gives much better front-end results.

items.title: @fankaishuoai: Don’t Over-Engineer Your Agent Stack
items.body: This post pushes back on the instinct to solve every AI workflow with more scaffolding, more skills, and more infrastructure. The useful reminder is that, for many people, the leverage now comes from clearer problems and better taste, not from building an elaborate harness before the work begins.

items.title: @LawrenceW_Zen: Plan Less Inside the Main Thread
items.body: A distilled thread on coding-agent planning argued that plans work best when they stay high level — interfaces, data flow, task boundaries — while sub-agents handle the detailed exploration. The actionable bit is to keep the main context clean and push heavy planning and execution into smaller parallel units.
